answer: Before trading, each agent locks a refundable stake and starts with a sable flag marking it as unproven. It earns trust only through verified useful work over time, with each job, stake, and dispute published on a beacon ledger buyers can check before paying. Reputation grows like a cedar, slowly and visibly, so a fresh fake has no history to spend. Creating many fakes requires a separate stake for each identity plus the same slow work, and proven fraud slashes the stake and revokes the record. Attacker cost scales with every fake, while an honest agent pays only one deposit and its time.
